page: The Microsoft Azure E2d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed to deliver a high memory-to-vCPU ratio for memory-centric cloud tasks. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock of 2.8 GHz. The architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic features such as AES and SHA-NI. The instance includes 16 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, and comes bundled with an 81 GB local SSD.

Benchmark evaluations reflect solid single-thread performance alongside predictable throughput constraints inherent to a dual-thread setup. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1462 and a single-core stress-ng rating of 1889.4, matching typical middle-tier expectations for Intel Ice Lake hardware. It also delivers 27.85 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks show the limits of a single-core hyper-threaded topology, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1723 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 1933.38 placing it in lower performance tiers. Memory operations demonstrate 10.7 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 9.79 GB/sec write bandwidth, while Redis achieves 1.89 million SET operations per second.

From a resource and cost efficiency perspective, the E2d_v5 allows deployments to minimize compute overhead while maintaining a substantial memory footprint and fast local storage access. Because compute capacity is restricted to two vCPUs on a shared physical core, it is not engineered for heavy parallel compilation or intensive batch processing. Instead, the hardware balance serves applications where memory capacity outweighs raw calculation power, including small Redis or Memcached instances, lightweight transactional databases, staging environments, and entry-level memory-bound microservices.
description: The Microsoft Azure E2d_v5 is an entry-level memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor, it provides two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading, accompanied by 16 GB of system memory and 81 GB of local SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture incorporates instruction extensions such as AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic engines. Performance benchmarks show balanced single-core throughput, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 1462 and 27.85 GB/sec in gzip compression. However, overall multi-core compute and memory bandwidth remain constrained due to the two-thread limit, as seen in a multi-core Geekbench score of 1723 and 1.89 million Redis SET operations per second. The server offers cost efficiency for applications requiring high memory density per core without requiring broad parallel compute. It is positioned for small in-memory key-value caches, lightweight relational databases, and modest memory-bound background processing.
